candidates.statement: A clinical trial’s eligibility criteria (inclusion and exclusion) are essential components of the trial, 28 defining the characteristics of the study population. 4 Because there is variability in 29 investigational drugs and trial objectives, eligibility criteria should be developed taking into 30 consideration the mechanism of action of the drug, the targeted disease or patient population, the 31 anticipated safety of the investigational drug, the availability of adequate safety data, and the 32
candidates.context: The purposes of eligibility criteria for cancer clinical trials are to select the intended patient 16 population and reduce potential risks to trial subjects. However, eligibility criteria are sometimes 17 more restrictive than necessary, and expanding eligibility criteria to be more representative is one 18 trial design consideration that may improve the applicability of clinical trial data to U.S. 19 populations. This guidance is one in a series of guidances that provide recommendations 20 regarding eligibility criteria for clinical trials of investigational drugs 2 regulated by CDER and 21 CBER for the treatment of cancer, although many of the concepts may apply more broadly to 22 other clinical areas. 3 Specifically, this guidance includes recommendations regarding expanding 23 eligibility criteria to include patients with a wider range of performance status . The Agency recognizes that some eligibility criteria may have become commonly accepted 34 over time or used as a template across trials, but such criteria should be carefully considered and 35 be appropriate for a specific trial context. Unnecessarily restrictive eligibility criteria may slow 36 subject accrual, limit patients’ access to clinical trials, and lead to trial results that do not fully 37 represent treatment effects in the patient population that will ultimately use the drug. 5 , 6

candidates.statement: Patients with ECOG PS2 (or KPS 60-70) should be included unless there is a scientific and/or 143 clinical rationale for exclusion justified by established safety considerations. Given the potential 144 for differences in AE rates, including PS2 patients could provide important safety data to 145 facilitate decision-making for patients in the post-approval setting. 146

candidates.statement: Where there are concerns regarding low PS based on the particular trial context, consider 171 alternative trial designs, such as pre-specified cohorts with low PS (ECOG ≥2 ) that are exempt 172 from the primary analysis, to encourage inclusion of these patients and collect safety data. These 173 cohorts would generally be small in size and exploratory in nature and could be enrolled 174 incrementally to enable an early stopping rule based upon safety data. Consideration of the data 175 analysis approach for the broader eligibility cohort and subgroup analysis should be determined 176 during the study design phase and its implications for marketing and post-marketing 177 requirements discussed with FDA when appropriate. Refer to FDA guidance for industry 178 Adaptive Design Clinical Trials for Drugs and Biologics (December 2019) when considering a 179 prespecified assessment of cohorts with low PS. 180

candidates.statement: Additional assessments of functional status should be considered to better characterize the 184 functional status of patients at baseline and over time. As with PS, these assessments should not 185 limit trial eligibility unless there is a scientific and/or clinical rationale for exclusion justified by 186 established safety considerations. 187
candidates.context: C. Recommendations for Additional Assessments of Functional Status 182 • Patient-generated physical function and activity data. Assessment of patient reported 189 physical function and role function, is recommended in FDA’s core patient-reported 190 outcomes in cancer clinical trials guidance 24 and can provide both baseline and 191 longitudinal data that can complement clinician-assessed PS. 25 Digital health 192 technologies (e.g., activity trackers) can also be explored to add additional objective 193 activity data to compare with clinician and patient report. 194
